name: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library – Durham County (Durham's Partnership for Children)
description: A free, age-appropriate book mailed to your child every month from birth until age 5. Run locally by Durham's Partnership for Children, the Durham County Smart Start agency.
address: 1201 S. Briggs Ave., Suite 100, Durham, NC 27703
access: All children from birth to age 5 who live in Durham County. No cost or obligation. Register online through Smart Start's Imagination Library page or mail or drop off the paper form.
notes: Contact: Jameka Wells, jameka@dpfc.net. Online registration: smartstart.org/dolly-partons-imagination-library/. Durham paused new enrollments in 2025 and reopened them after new state funding in July 2026; the Imagination Library's Durham affiliate page says it is now accepting new registrations.

name: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library – Wake County (Wake County Smart Start)
description: A free new book mailed to your child each month until their 5th birthday. Run locally by Wake County Smart Start. The first book should arrive 8–10 weeks after you register.
address: 4901 Waters Edge Dr., Suite 101, Raleigh, NC 27606
access: Any child under 5 who lives in Wake County. Books are mailed only to Wake County addresses. Enroll online or mail in the bilingual paper form.
notes: Wake County Smart Start says registration has reopened after the 2025 pause. Contact: Denise Rossi, drossi@wakesmartstart.org; general line (919) 851-9550. If you move, update your address, because books can take 10–12 weeks to start at the new address.

name: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library – Orange County (Orange County Partnership for Young Children)
description: A free book mailed to registered children each month from birth to age 5. Run locally by the Orange County Partnership for Young Children, Orange County's Smart Start agency.
access: Children from birth to age 5 living in Orange County. Enroll online through Smart Start's Imagination Library page.
notes: The partnership says registrations, paused in 2025, have resumed. For address changes, contact Jaida Grant at (984) 677-2215 or jgrant@orangesmartstart.org. General email: ocpyc@orangesmartstart.org.

name: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library – Chatham County (Chatham County Partnership for Children)
description: A new book in the mail every month at no cost to Chatham County children from birth until their 5th birthday. Run by the Chatham County Partnership for Children (Smart Start).
access: Chatham County children from birth until their 5th birthday. Register online (imaginationlibrary.com/usa/affiliate/NCPCCHATHAMCO/) or with the printable form. Register at least 10 weeks before the child turns 5.
notes: Funded by the NC Legislature and local partners. Main office: (919) 542-7449.

name: Wake County Smart Start – Wake Connections (free parent support & home visiting)
description: A single free application that connects Wake County families with free home-visiting and parent-group support programs, from pregnancy to age 5. Wake County Smart Start also runs a searchable Family Support Connection Tool and Wake Pre-K / ThreeSchool.
address: 4901 Waters Edge Dr., Suite 101, Raleigh, NC 27606
access: Wake County families who are pregnant or postpartum, or have children from birth to age 5. Families can apply themselves through the confidential online form, or by phone if they don't have internet. The programs it refers to are free for eligible families.
notes: Email info@wakesmartstart.org. Free Wake Pre-K (4-year-olds) and Wake ThreeSchool (3-year-olds) for eligible children: wakesmartstart.org/wake-pre-k/.

name: Chatham County Partnership for Children – Family Resource Center (child care search & Ch.A.M.P.S. diapers)
description: The Family Resource Center gives free, confidential child care referrals to licensed and many license-exempt programs in Chatham County, including evening or overnight care and programs with transportation. Its Ch.A.M.P.S. program gives free diapers, wipes and hygiene products to families with young children.
hours: Phone line Mon–Fri 8am–5pm. Calls are returned within one business day.
access: Chatham County families with young children. Families can call themselves or search for child care online. Ch.A.M.P.S. is for Chatham families in need; call to request supplies.
notes: Ch.A.M.P.S. contact: Steffanny Dubon, bilingual family outreach coordinator, (984) 214-2407 (chathamkids.org/chathams-assistance-for-maternal-and-pediatric-supplies-ch-a-m-p-s/). The partnership is also an official car seat checking station, by appointment at its office; the page doesn't state a cost. Main line (919) 542-7449.

name: Kaleidoscope Play and Learn (Chatham County Partnership for Children)
description: Free weekly playgroups for children from birth to 5 and their caregivers. Children play while caregivers connect with each other and learn about child development and kindergarten-readiness skills. Includes a story time.
address: Chatham Community Library, 197 NC-87, Pittsboro, NC 27312
hours: Pittsboro: Wednesdays, sessions 10–11am and 11:30am–12:30pm, story time 11–11:30am
access: Parents and caregivers of children from birth to 5 who don't attend preschool or child care.
notes: Also meets Thursdays 10–11:30am at Wren Memorial Library in Siler City and Fridays 10–11:30am at Goldston Library. Bilingual contact: Cyntia Gutierrez, (984) 214-2360.

name: Early Years (formerly Child Care Services Association) – Child Care Scholarships & Referrals
description: Locally funded child care scholarships that help Durham and Orange County families pay for 4- or 5-star licensed child care, birth to age 5. Referral specialists also give personalized referrals to local child care programs and explain NC's star-rating system.
address: 1829 E. Franklin St., Suite 1000, Chapel Hill, NC 27514
access: Scholarships: Durham or Orange County families with children from birth to 5. Each parent must need full-time care (usually 30+ hours of work or school a week) and be under the income limit (e.g. family of 3: Durham $93,598, Orange $130,715). Families are screened, then invited to apply. The waitlist is ranked by income per family member, with priority for homelessness and teen parents.
notes: Scholarship line: toll-free 855-EARLY-ED (855-327-5933), familyscholarship@earlyyearsnc.org. Spanish-speaking staff available. Durham office: 1201 S. Briggs Ave., Suite 200, Durham 27703. Main line (919) 967-3272. Child care referrals: earlyyearsnc.org/programs/ccrr/; the page doesn't state whether referrals are free.

name: Family Connects Durham (free newborn nurse home visit)
description: A free visit from a registered nurse for every family with a newborn in Durham County, usually about 3 weeks after birth. The nurse checks the baby's health and weight and the parent's recovery, helps with breastfeeding, and connects families to child care, financial help, parenting classes and postpartum depression support. Visits can be at home, at another location, or by phone or video.
address: 1121 W. Chapel Hill St., Suite 100, Durham, NC 27701
access: All Durham County parents of newborns up to 12 weeks old, regardless of income. No charge. Nurses do not ask about or report residency status. If your baby was born outside Durham, sign up online or by phone.
notes: Formerly Durham Connects. Run by the Center for Child & Family Health with Duke, the Durham County Health Department and Durham County DSS. Spanish-speaking nurses or an in-person interpreter are available. Sign up at ccfhnc.org/fcd-sign-up/.

name: Kramden Institute – Free Computers for Students & Low-Cost Computers
description: Refurbished computers for families: free computers for K–12 students without a working home computer, and $40 desktops (monitor included) or $70 laptops for low-income adults, with Windows 11 and a 90-day warranty. Also free online Northstar digital-skills classes and public community sales of low-cost equipment.
access: Students: grades K–12 without consistent access to a working home computer. A parent or educator can apply online in English or Spanish; one computer per household; typical wait 2–4 weeks. Adults: below 200% of the poverty level or enrolled in SNAP, Medicaid, disability or similar benefits, with proof of eligibility; wait about 4–8 weeks. Pickup in Durham only, no shipping.
notes: Adult program: kramden.org/get-tech/computers-for-low-income-adults/. Community sales are open to the public, Thursdays 4–5pm every 3–4 weeks (kramden.org/community-sales-ebay/). Email info@kramden.org.

name: Kidznotes – Durham Nucleo (low-cost after-school orchestra)
description: After-school classical music instruction (strings, winds, percussion) for students in grades 3–12. Accepted students get an instrument and supplies to use while enrolled. Levels run from beginner Explorers to auditioned high-school Maestros.
address: Fayetteville Street Elementary, 2905 Fayetteville St., Durham, NC 27707
access: Students in grades 3–12. No experience is needed for beginner levels; intermediate levels need an application and assessment, and Maestros need an audition. One-time annual fee of $50 ($25 for each additional child); payment plans on request.
notes: Registration for new students is closed now; the Nucleo page says spring-semester registration reopens in November 2026. Optional electives cost $25. Kidznotes also runs the Mozart violin program for 1st–2nd graders at partner schools, with priority for families eligible for free or reduced lunch. Office: 1309 Halley St., Durham.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Wake County – Raleigh Clubs
description: After-school and summer youth programs, mentoring and a safe place for ages 6–18. Raleigh has a Boys Club (605 N. Raleigh Blvd.), a Girls Club (701 N. Raleigh Blvd.) and The Club Teen Center for high schoolers (721 N. Raleigh Blvd.).
hours: Mon–Fri 2:30–8pm during the school year; teacher workdays 8am–6pm
access: Youth ages 6–18. The Boys Club takes new members age 6 through 8th grade, the Girls Club ages 6–14, and the Teen Center grades 9–12. Membership is $7.50 a year. Call the club to register.
notes: Girls Club (919) 821-9191; Teen Center (919) 250-3595. Other Wake clubs: Washington Elementary, Fox Road and Parrish Manor (Raleigh), plus Zebulon and Wake Forest. Parent portal: bgcwakecounty.my.site.com/portal/s/.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Wake County – Zebulon Club
description: After-school and summer youth programs with mentors, for East Wake youth.
hours: Mon–Fri 2:30–8pm during the school year; teacher workdays 8am–6pm
access: Youth ages 6–18. Membership is $7.50 a year.
notes: The $7.50 annual fee is listed on wakejohnstonbgc.org.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Wake County – Wake Forest Club
description: After-school and summer youth programs with mentors.
address: 325 S. Wingate St., Wake Forest, NC 27587
hours: Mon–Fri 2:30–8pm during the school year; teacher workdays 8am–6pm
access: Youth ages 6–18. Membership is $7.50 a year.
notes: The $7.50 annual fee is listed on wakejohnstonbgc.org.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Durham and Orange Counties
description: After-school program every weekday of the school year, plus summer camp and athletics, for ages 6–18. Clubs in Durham and Chapel Hill.
address: 1010 Martin Luther King Jr. Pkwy., Suite 300, Durham, NC 27713
hours: Weekdays during the school year (after school)
access: Youth ages 6–18; 18-year-olds must still be in high school. Durham membership is $10 a year. Apply with the 2026–27 paper application (English or Spanish) and attach the child's last report card.
notes: Optional school-bus pickup to the Durham club costs extra ($130 per child, per the application). The Chapel Hill club is at 505 Craig St. (Craig Gomains), Chapel Hill 27516; its application doesn't state the fee, so call to confirm.

name: Museum of Life and Science – Durham Community Days (free admission)
description: Free admission to Durham's hands-on science museum, with outdoor exhibits, a butterfly house and animals, for Durham County residents on several Community Days a year.
hours: 10am–5pm on Community Days. Remaining 2026 dates: Tue Nov 17, Wed Dec 2, Sun Dec 13.
access: Durham County residents with current proof of a Durham address. Every adult must show Durham residency, and each adult can bring up to five children. Visitors without proof pay regular admission.
notes: Children 2 and under are always free. Regular admission is $19–24.

name: Chapel Hill Fire Department – Free Car Seat Checks
description: A free weekly car seat clinic where trained child passenger safety technicians check car seat installation and show you how to install it.
address: Fire Station 2, 1003 S. Hamilton Rd., Chapel Hill, NC
access: Open to anyone, no appointment needed. If you can't come Saturday, you can request another time through the town's online form.
notes: Call the phone number during business hours.
